decisions.decision: Repository facts and scoped reading routes replace dependence on conversation memory.
decisions.reason: New chats must restart cheaply without importing old speculation or forgetting unresolved failures.
decisions.tradeoff: Maintained cards and checkpoints need small updates alongside meaningful code changes.

decisions.decision: Bridge and managed game keep distinct identities, source roots and context packets.
decisions.reason: Changing development infrastructure must not be confused with editing the simulated game.
decisions.tradeoff: Desktop game-pack integration is a separate tracked task (PACK-1).

decisions.decision: Full changed files are staged against exact base revision/hashes before promotion.
decisions.reason: Avoid fuzzy patches, accidental live overwrite and incorrect-base updates.
decisions.tradeoff: Hashes prevent some drift; they do not prove code correctness or authenticate the author. Crash safety still requires SAFE-1.

decisions.decision: Hard checks cover objective structural errors; size and freshness remain review signals.
decisions.reason: Protection must not freeze user-directed design or impose bureaucracy on every cosmetic edit.
decisions.tradeoff: Semantic consistency still requires developer review. Deliberate redesign updates decisions, interfaces and tests together.

decisions.decision: One shared coordinator commits source/build pairs for init, repair, update and rollback, with before-images addressed by unique transaction identity.
decisions.reason: Crash recovery must not depend on duplicated UI-specific promotion paths or stale numeric revision snapshots. Tests use the same Rust library as the app.
decisions.tradeoff: Retained snapshots consume disk. Legacy incomplete journals stop safely rather than inferring intent. Process-death tests are not physical power-loss or sandbox certification.

decisions.decision: All short-lived Godot work uses a parent-owned deadline, bounded pipe capture and whole-worker-tree containment. Ordinary Play stays untimed.
decisions.reason: Engine iteration limits cannot recover a hung process; closing a console launcher is insufficient when its child keeps running. Recovery must confirm worker quiescence before modifying staging.
decisions.tradeoff: Windows job APIs require Windows 10+; Linux support is CI/normal process-group supervision, not persistent parent-death containment. This is trusted-code lifecycle control, not a security sandbox.

decisions.decision: Installer acceptance runs the actual packaged desktop app with bundled resources in a new isolated workspace before publishing its artifact.
decisions.reason: A source-tree E2E cannot establish correct resource packaging, native frontend IPC, install paths or uninstall behavior. Cargo metadata and exact provenance bind evidence to the delivered installer.
decisions.tradeoff: PR checks take longer but produce a tested development artifact. The opt-in probe is not exhaustive user interaction, a pristine Windows image or code signing.
